name: Otis Worldwide
description: Otis builds, installs and services elevators and escalators. It makes its money in two very different ways: selling new equipment (low margin, 35 percent of sales) and servicing about 2.5 million units under maintenance contracts (65 percent of sales, and about 91 percent of segment profit). Contracts renew repeatedly, the maintenance portfolio includes rivals' equipment, and about 1.1 million units are remotely connected. Roughly half of global service units are held by independent small operators, which Otis targets for conversion. Customers are building developers, contractors and governments (new equipment) and building owners (service and modernisation).

sub.name: Heating, cooling, elevators, lighting and building controls

employees.note: About 72,000 colleagues including about 45,000 field professionals; 45 percent in Asia, 34 percent in EMEA, 21 percent in the Americas.

businessLines.name: Service
businessLines.how: Annual maintenance and repair contracts on about 2.5 million elevators and escalators (Otis and other makers), plus modernisation projects that replace aging units; recurring contract revenue that grows by converting newly installed units and winning units from other service providers.

businessLines.name: New Equipment
businessLines.how: Sells and installs new elevators and escalators to developers, contractors and governments, delivered generally within 12 months of order (shorter in China); one-time project sales whose main purpose is to feed the later service portfolio.

brands.name: Otis
brands.note: Single brand; Otis equipment and other makers' units in the maintenance portfolio
